name: Southeast Route
descent_text: Reverse the ridge and boot track to La Bohn Gap, downclimbing the class 2 to 3 rock, which is loose throughout. From the gap descend to the valley floor by the boulder gully, by the waterfall route beside it, or by the snow chute when it is soft; hard early-season snow calls for an axe and crampons. Then follow Necklace Valley trail past the lakes, down the steep 2,400 ft switchbacks to the footlog across the East Fork Foss River, and out the five gentle miles to the trailhead.
approach: Park at the Necklace Valley (East Fork Foss) trailhead at the end of FR 68 and follow the East Fork Foss trail up the valley. The first five miles are gentle forest, gaining only about 600 ft, until a footlog crossing of the East Fork Foss River, then the trail climbs about 2,400 ft in three miles of steep, rooty switchbacks to Jade Lake and on up the Necklace Valley past the other lakes. Leave the valley trail at its upper end, where the hanging valley leads to La Bohn Lakes and the climb proper. Camps at the lakes or in Necklace Valley make this a two-day trip for most parties. From the end of the valley, climb the boulder gully or the waterfall route to La Bohn Gap (about 6,000 ft); the snow chute is the early-season option and needs an axe. The route starts from the gap, where a clear climbers' boot track turns north.
